name: Borden Tunnel
facts: Borden Tunnel, a 957‑foot long passage, was constructed in 1911 by the Western Maryland Railway to serve its Connellsville Subdivision, linking freight routes across the Allegheny Mountains.
After the rail line was abandoned in 1975, Borden Tunnel was repurposed for the Great Allegheny Passage rail trail, now illuminated by motion‑activated LED lights powered by a nearby solar panel.
The tunnel’s 957‑foot length makes it a modest yet iconic feature of the trail, showcasing early 20th‑century engineering that still supports modern recreational use.
